title: Twitter/X canonical capture (v1)
description: One acquisition of one public X post or same-author self-thread, normalized away from every provider's response shape. Delivered by T-223 and frozen on the measurements in docs/spikes/T-222/REPORT.md, not on any provider's documentation — that report records four places where the candidate tool's own field table disagreed with what it returned. Extraction and UI consume this record; they never see a provider response (ADR 0007 decision 7). Every constraint below exists to make a specific dishonest record unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged, so the reasons are recorded inline.

raw_evidence.description: One entry per route actually read. Immutable: a later capture never rewrites an earlier one (ADR 0007 invariant 3).

items.description: The captured posts in root-first order. Order is asserted by 'order', never by position alone.

postId.$comment: String, never a number: T-222 observed both '20' and '2094037638856454625', and the larger exceeds a double's exact-integer range, so any numeric handling would silently corrupt it. Narrow to digits because every id observed was numeric; the v1 README permits widening a pattern in place, so a future non-numeric id costs an edit rather than a version.

tier.$comment: 0 and 1 only. Tier 2 is session cookies, which ADR 0007 decision 6 excludes, so a capture that claims it is unrepresentable rather than merely disallowed by policy.

surface.$comment: The named surfaces T-222 actually exercised. A capture must say which one filled it, because the same field arrives complete or truncated depending on the surface (REPORT.md section 5).

provenance.description: Which route, tier and surface produced a value.

provider.description: The externally installed, pinned tool. Never vendored; never a build dependency (D-208).

network.$comment: D-209: the qualified path is used over an always-on tunnel, which is a named environment dependency of Phase 2.2. Recorded per capture so a later reachability failure can be told apart from provider drift instead of being blamed on the provider.

routeRead.description: One request actually made. A failed read is recorded, not dropped: an outage that leaves no trace is indistinguishable from a route never tried.

outcome.$comment: 'rate_limited' and 'timeout' are named because T-222 measured them as distinct, deterministic exits (5 and 8). A transport failure must never be scored as evidence about a capability.

request_shape.$comment: The argv or URL shape, with any request token stripped. Never a credential, never a cookie (ADR 0007 invariant 1).

path.description: Project-relative path to the preserved bytes. Forward slashes; no absolute path, no parent traversal.

sha256_raw.$comment: The digest BEFORE sanitization, kept alongside the sanitized one so a redaction cannot be passed off as the original bytes (REPORT.md section 8).

sanitization_removed.$comment: What redaction actually removed. An empty array is a real, meaningful claim here — 'nothing matched' — unlike the absent-not-empty fields on a post, because sanitization always ran.

anchor.description: The reference the user supplied, and what role it plays in the thread.

terminal_claim.$comment: D-206. Nothing credential-free proves an anchor is a thread's last post, so the basis is recorded and 'observed' is not an option. 'user_asserted' is the contract's normal case; 'none' means no terminal claim is made at all.

textEntity.description: A span inside the canonical text, plus what it points at. D-211: the expanded target lives here, never substituted into the text.

expanded.$comment: A provider's expansion of a t.co link. Kept beside the span because T-222 measured one expansion that was LONGER than the authored link, so substituting it would shift every subsequent offset in a stored corpus without the post changing (REPORT.md section 5a).

canonical.$comment: The authored form, t.co links intact (D-211). Every span in this capture and every locator downstream is an offset into this string.

completeness.$comment: Text completeness has no in-band signal on any measured route, so it is never asserted from one read. Tier 0 returned 280 of 3659 characters with no field announcing the loss, so 'unverified' is the honest default and 'corroborated' requires a second route that agreed.

agreement.$comment: URL-normalized comparison. A raw comparison disagreed on three of four Persian posts purely over link representation, so a raw check would fire on almost every post carrying media or a URL (REPORT.md section 5a).

url.$comment: Metadata and a stable-as-available URL. Binary preservation is out of ADR 0007's MVP scope, and these hosts expire, so a reader must treat this as decaying.

alt_text.$comment: Author-written. Real and worth carrying: 62 of 108 media objects observed had it. Absent when the author wrote none — never an empty string standing in for one.

metrics.$comment: ADR 0007: a metric is only meaningful as an explicitly time-stamped observation, so observed_at is required and every count is optional. A capture therefore cannot carry a bare number that a reader would compare across time as though it were a property of the post.

reason.$comment: Tier 0 and Tier 1 collapse deleted, suspended and protected into one message; x routes puts distinguishable errors at Tier 2, which is excluded. So the only honest value at a qualified tier is 'not_determinable_at_this_tier'. The specific reasons are listed but unreachable without a tier that can tell them apart, which is the point.

conversation_id.$comment: Optional by measurement, not by preference: a Tier 0 single-post read returns null for it, so a capture taken at Tier 0 legitimately cannot name the conversation it walked (REPORT.md section 7).

parent_post_id.description: The post this one replies to. Present for every thread member except the root.

media.$comment: Absent when the post carries none. An empty array would claim 'observed, and there was none', which a truncating surface cannot support.

quote.$comment: A quoted post is a separate cited source, not embedded content (ADR 0007 decision 8). Its id and author are available at Tier 0, so both are required when a quote is recorded at all.

poll.$comment: T-222 located no public poll in 610 credential-free posts and the tool declares 'poll' with no surface at any tier. So a poll is representable but only as a real observation: minProperties forbids recording {} as though absence had been observed. Same doctrine for edits, article and reply_settings below (REPORT.md section 9).

basis.$comment: Order is derived from parent links and never from the order records arrived in: the archive route returns a ranked selection, so arrival order carries no chronological meaning at all (REPORT.md section 4).

completeness.$comment: Kept separate from request success, and directional, because T-222 measured the two directions as different kinds of claim: upward is provable by termination at a parent-less root, downward is not provable by any credential-free route.

basis.$comment: 'root_reached' means a post with no parent was reached and every hop resolved — the one real completeness proof available. 'unresolved_hop' names the id that broke the chain.

status.$comment: 'unprovable' is the only honest value at a qualified tier and there is deliberately no 'complete': x thread and x replies return the anchor alone, the whole reply tree is Tier 2, and a 250-post author archive held 3 of 10 members of a real thread. A capture cannot claim it enumerated descendants.

coverage.$comment: Item-based, per ADR 0007 and the T-223 row: every included post is accounted for and every omission carries a reason. PASS while an expected item is unaccounted for is impossible — JSON Schema cannot compare two arrays, so that bound is asserted in tests/test_twitter_capture_schema.py, in the same way the extraction bundle's window bounds are.

descriptor.description: Used when the omitted item has no known id — a descendant that cannot be enumerated has no id to name.
